identity.title: POCUS cardiac: RV dilation (RV:LV >1), septal flattening, McConnell sign

technique.how: Phased-array probe; obtain apical 4-chamber (plus parasternal long/short axis and subcostal). Compare RV to LV end-diastolic basal diameter: RV:LV >1 = dilated. Look for interventricular septal flattening/paradoxical motion (D-shaped LV in short axis) and McConnell sign (RV free-wall akinesis with preserved apical motion).
technique.prerequisites: Trained operator with cardiac POCUS competence; adequate apical window (foreshortening exaggerates or hides RV size).
technique.contraindications: None; do not delay treatment of an unstable patient for image acquisition.

interpretation.positive_finding: RV dilation (RV:LV >1) in a patient with moderate/high pretest probability is highly specific for PE (98% in Dresden 2014; LR+ 29) and, with shock, supports thrombolysis decisions; McConnell sign and septal flattening were seen only in PE patients in that cohort.
interpretation.negative_finding: Normal RV size does not exclude PE: sensitivity is ~50% (pooled 53% for 'right heart strain'), so a negative scan should not stop CTPA or D-dimer-based workup.
interpretation.pitfalls: Chronic pulmonary hypertension, COPD, RV infarct and ARDS also dilate the RV; RV dilation is a marker of large PE, not of PE in general. Foreshortened apical views and off-axis cuts misjudge RV:LV ratio.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive with shock: treat as massive PE (anticoagulate; consider lysis/embolectomy); positive without shock: proceed to CTPA and risk-stratify; negative: continue standard PE workup.

estimates.target_condition: Pulmonary embolism; finding = right ventricular dilatation (RV:LV >1:1) on EP bedside echo
estimates.population: 146 ED patients with suspected (moderate-high pretest probability) or confirmed PE; 30 had PE
estimates.reference_standard: Final radiology reading of CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q scan (chart review)
estimates.quote: Positive and negative likelihood ratios were determined to be 29 (95% CI 6.1% to 64%) and 0.51 (95% CI 0.4% to 0.7%)
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (sens 50% [32-68], spec 98% [95-100] in preceding sentence of the abstract)

estimates.target_condition: Pulmonary embolism; finding = undefined 'right heart strain' on transthoracic echo
estimates.population: Pooled systematic review of TTE diagnostic-accuracy studies for PE through 2016 (various operators, ED/ICU/inpatient)
estimates.reference_standard: CT pulmonary angiography or other confirmatory imaging per study
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.53/(1-0.83); LR- = (1-0.53)/0.83 from pooled sens/spec in abstract
estimates.quote: it had a sensitivity of 53% (95% CI, 45%-61%) and a specificity of 83% (95% CI, 74%-90%)

sources.citation: Dresden S, Mitchell P, Rahimi L, et al. Right ventricular dilatation on bedside echocardiography performed by emergency physicians aids in the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism. Ann Emerg Med. 2014;63(1):16-24.
Fields JM, Davis J, Girson L, et al. Transthoracic Echocardiography for Diagnosing Pulmonary Embolism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Am Soc Echocardiogr. 2017;30(7):714-723.e4.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a normal RV to exclude PE; do not attribute RV dilation to PE without considering chronic pulmonary hypertension, COPD or RV infarction, especially when the RV wall is thickened.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: RV dilation with hypotension or syncope in suspected PE indicates massive/high-risk PE: immediate anticoagulation and reperfusion decision (lysis or embolectomy) without waiting for CTPA if unstable.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Dresden 2014 reported 96% observed agreement between co-investigators and the principal investigator on recorded images; Fields 2017 found signs inconsistently defined across studies ('undefined right heart strain' most common).
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency physician credentialed in focused cardiac ultrasound with adequate apical 4-chamber acquisition; the Dresden cohort used trained EP investigators in a convenience sample enriched for moderate/high pretest probability.

extraction_notes: Dresden 2014 provides the RV:LV >1 estimate with CIs directly from the abstract (the abstract prints LR CIs with stray '%' signs, transcribed as ratios). Fields 2017 abstract only quantifies the undefined 'right heart strain' sign (LRs computed here); per-sign pooled values for RV:LV ratio, septal motion and McConnell sign are in full-text tables that are not open access, so they are not extracted. McConnell/septal flattening in Dresden were 6/6 and 8/8 PE-positive: too few to give sens/spec, described in prose only.
